items.title: A second opinion is only useful if it is independent
items.body: The host's point is that two of the leading model families now give much the same answer in different words, and a third that reasons differently is worth consulting for that reason alone. Medicine knows this well: a second opinion from someone trained in the same firm adds less than one from elsewhere. For a hard problem, asking a differently built model is reasonable, provided no patient-identifiable data goes into a tool the practice has not approved.

items.title: A model that caves when challenged is unsafe for checking
items.body: The reported flaw matters clinically. This model abandons its answer at the slightest pushback, then reverses again if pushed the other way. A tool that agrees with whoever spoke last cannot be used to check your own reasoning, because it will confirm it. Treat its first, unprompted answer as the only informative one.

items.title: Agentic hacking tools and practice security
items.body: A freely available automated hacking tool has been linked to a breach at the European Commission that took out payroll. Small organisations with old systems are the easy targets. The basics still do most of the work: multi-factor authentication on NHSmail and the clinical system, prompt patching, and a tested offline fallback. Ed Zitron has published nothing on this model, so there is no opposing source today.
